subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This chooses a scheduled-run security boundary and public config/default contract, including compatibility for cron jobs that currently use direct message sends.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions too, reducing config surface while coupling two execution modes.

options.title: Keep per-job policy only
options.body: Avoid new global cron config and rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery safeguards for scheduled runs.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.
